chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Supplication is the shield of the believer, and whenever you knock frequently on a door, it will be opened for you.'

key_terms.الدعاء: Du'a — supplication, invocation; distinguished from formal salat by its personal, conversational quality
key_terms.تُرْس: Turs — a round shield (lighter than mijann); the metaphor implies du'a actively deflects harm
key_terms.قَرْع الباب: Knocking on the door — a proverbial expression for persistent supplication; the 'door' is God's mercy

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the role of supplication (du'a) in a believer's life?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) quotes Imam Ali (AS) using a powerful military metaphor: du'a is a shield (turs) that protects the believer against calamities. The accompanying proverb — persistent knocking opens the door — emphasizes that sincere, repeated supplication is answered by God. This teaching was addressed to believers who might neglect du'a during times of ease, reminding them that it is both a protective weapon and a means of drawing close to God through persistence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘The supplication is a shield of the Momin, and when the door is knocked upon frequently, it would be opened for you’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘Prayer is a shield for a believing person. When a door is knocked often it will sooner or later open up.’”
